correctness.rationale: For two independent uniform interior points the normalized difference density is product_i(a_i-|z_i|)_+/vol(Q)^2. Substitute z=Ry with R^d/vol(Q)=1/omega_d; below rho<min a_i/R the positive factors expand to finitely many elementary symmetric sums. Integrals of k distinct coordinate absolute values over a Euclidean rho-ball equal pi^((d-k)/2)rho^(d+k)/Gamma(1+(d+k)/2), giving every claimed coefficient with no remainder. The normalization fixes e_d(b)=1/omega_d, so the leading 1 and coefficients k=1,...,d-1 determine every coefficient of prod(z-b_i), including repeated positive roots. Perturbing e_{m+1} at distinct simple roots while fixing lower e_k and the constant term proves fewer measurements fail locally. Rouché applied to radius delta^(1/d) unions of root disks gives a uniform multiset matching; reciprocals are Lipschitz for b>=u. Perturb two real-rooted monic polynomials only in their constant terms, shift roots by epsilon and normalize products, yielding a coefficient gap O(epsilon^d) but root gap Theta(epsilon), so exponent 1/d is sharp at cubes. Independent normalized coefficients and fixed-product checks passed in d=3,4,5,7; these do not certify the general statement.
residual_risks: The exact polynomial is only valid below the first width threshold.
Rouché constants depend on fixed dimension and compact positive shape bounds; finite-sample inference is not asserted.

value.rationale: A finite-radius local distance profile is an intrinsic similarity-invariant observation model for boxes. Exact identification by d-1 coefficients, proof no fewer suffice, and sharp non-Lipschitz stability at repeated roots solve a natural complete inverse problem, rather than an arbitrary cut of a known table. Its optimal root-collision exponent quantifies the instability of nearly cubical shapes; no downstream reconstruction algorithm or large application is needed for this intrinsic fact.
residual_risks: Only exact population germs, not finite-sample or noise-optimal statistics, are covered.
